title: Cell potential, free energy and the Nernst equation
competency: Relate E°cell to ΔG° and K, and use the Nernst equation for non-standard cells, concentration cells and pH.

keywords.def: The potential difference that drives electrons from anode to cathode, in volts.
Two identical half-cells with different concentrations; E°cell = 0.

ideas.name: Cell potential, free energy and K

en.text: A cell's EMF is linked to free energy by ΔG = −nFE: a positive cell potential means a negative ΔG and a spontaneous reaction. At standard conditions ΔG° = −nFE° and ΔG° = −RT ln K, so at 25 °C log K = nE°/0.0592 and ln K = nE°/0.0257. A large positive E° means a very large K.

am.text: ΔG = −nFE፤ አዎንታዊ E አሉታዊ ΔG ማለት ድንገተኛ ነው። ΔG° = −RT ln K፤ log K = nE°/0.0592።

en.text: Real cells are not at 1 M. The Nernst equation corrects for concentration: Ecell = E°cell − (0.0592/n) log Q at 25 °C. As a cell runs, products build up, Q rises and Ecell falls until it reaches 0 at equilibrium (a dead battery). A concentration cell has identical half-cells; its E° is 0, but different concentrations still give a voltage. The same idea lets a cell measure pH.

am.text: የኔርንስት እኩልታ፡ Ecell = E°cell − (0.0592/n) log Q። ሴሉ ሲሠራ Q ይጨምራል፣ E ይቀንሳል፤ በሚዛን ዜሮ ይሆናል።

screens.title: The Nernst equation
paras: ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q gives Ecell = E°cell − (RT/nF) ln Q.
As the cell runs, Q rises and Ecell falls.
At equilibrium Ecell = 0, ΔG = 0 and Q = K: the battery is dead.

screens.title: Concentration cells and pH

Dilute side is the anode; concentrated side is the cathode.
With a Zn electrode and a hydrogen electrode in the test solution: pH = (0.76 − Ecell)/0.0592.

notes.text: p.111, Example 2.11 and p.116–117 call the concentration ratio "K"; with non-equilibrium concentrations it is the reaction quotient Q. Gases enter Q as pressures in atm (p.111 converts to mol/L, which is not the usual convention).
Example 2.8: the anode is Sn → Sn²⁺ + 2e⁻ (book "Sn⁺"). Example 2.9: Au³⁺/Au, not Au²⁺/Au. Exercise 2.10: silver ion is Ag⁺, not "Ag²⁺". Exercise 2.11 Q2: E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V.
p.109: electrons flow from the anode (−) to the cathode (+); the book's "higher potential" wording mixes conventions. Figure 2.15b labels "Anode (−)" for an electrolytic cell; it should be (+).
The pH-from-Ecell item (0.523 V → pH 4.0) is an added example.
